meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Federal state comprising Common Law jurisdictions; Quebec applies Civil Law for private matters)

Convention on the Recognition and Enforcement of Foreign Arbitral Awards (New York Convention)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), S.C. 2000, c. 17; Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1 (Quebec Registry of Enterprises); Quebec Regulations respecting the information to be published by legal persons and partnerships; Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46; Canadian sanctions under the Special Economic Measures Act (SEMA) and United Nations Act.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Fully_Public (available to the public upon written request to the Registraire des entreprises; UBO declarations filed within 30 days of any change)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Legal Existence / Certificate of Good Standing from jurisdiction of ultimate parent or foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Original company registry (e.g., home jurisdiction Ministry of Corporate Affairs)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (for documents issued in contracting states; Canada acceded 11 May 2024 immediate application to foreign-source documents)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified True Copies of Passport and Proof of Residential Address (Directors and all Ultimate Beneficial Owners)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the jurisdiction of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization + Hague Apostille certificate (Consular legalization if not an Apostille member state)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Limited Partnership Agreement (LPA) and Articles of Formation (for LP registration)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if issued abroad) or certified by a Quebec notary when executed locally

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all partners and UBOs against OSC, UN, OFAC SDN, EU, and Canadian sanctions lists; mandatory PEP review under FINTRAC directives; enhanced due diligence (EDD) for foreign-source funds in offshore towage/salvage transactions, including direct analysis of source of wealth and source of funds; ongoing transaction monitoring aligned with PCMLTFA risk-assessment requirements.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises de Quebec (REQ) through Services Quebec online portal (www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Pursuant to the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c. C-11), all LP names must be registered in French. A non-French name is permitted if a previously registered French version exists and the non-French name is used in a context where an equivalent French name is also used; transliteration must respect recognized linguistic conventions and cannot rely on arbitrary Latin or transliteration schemes.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A written appeal citing grounds of fact and law may be filed with the Director of the Registraire des entreprises within 60 days from rejection, followed by an administrative review and, if unresolved, an application for Judicial Review at the Monetary and Administrative Tribunal of Quebec (TAM) with legal costs estimate in budget.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible with restrictions: the registered office must retain a physical, street-level address in Quebec capable of receiving original served documents; strictly virtual mailbox-only addresses are insufficient and will be rejected during registry examination.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (below 5% baseline) for pure holding LP; Medium_High if vessels call at Port of Montreal or Saint-Laurent waterway where Canadian Transport Canada may conduct compliance review; the offshore towage/salvage character increases the probability of a targeted AML/CFT review when engaging with flagged high-risk counterparties.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec, arts. 2236-2246 (société en commandite); Act respecting the Legal Publicity of Enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, ss. 2(4), 12-13, 20, 28-32; no CBCA incorporation applies because a Quebec Limited Partnership is a contractual partnership with limited liability of its commanditaires
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - Directeur de l'immatriculation, Service de l'immatriculation, Québec City
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation (Declaration of Registration) filed under s. 12 of the Act respecting the Legal Publicity of Enterprises
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None (Quebec Limited Partnerships have no statutory minimum paid-up capital; capital is fixed by the partnership agreement and may be cash, property, or services; no REQ escrow mandate exists, but a contractual escrow/retention fund is customary for Lloyd's salvage contracts)
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA RESOLUTION OF THE GENERAL PARTNER (COMMANDITÉ) ADOPTED BY UNANIMOUS WRITTEN CONSENT OF THE BOARD OF GENERAL PARTNER INC.: (1) The subscribers named in the Limited Partnership Agreement are admitted as limited partners (commanditaires) and their subscribed capital contributions are recorded in the partnership ledger; (2) The registered office of the Partnership is established at 1000 Rue de la Gauchetière Ouest, Montréal, Québec H3B 5H4 and the Registraire des entreprises du Québec is confirmed as the registration authority; (3) The Secretary is appointed to execute and file the Declaration of Registration under the Act respecting the Legal Publicity of Enterprises and to open the Partnership's bank accounts; (4) Any officer is authorized to approve Lloyds wire instructions, escrow mandates, and annual operating permits.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - Online Name Verification Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a preliminary designation search via REQ online portal using the mandatory legal ending 'société en commandite' or 'S.E.C.'; submit a name verification request identifying the General Partner, its registered office, and three proposed designations in order of preference; the REQ system issues a name availability opinion and reserves an approved designation for 60 days.
required_dossiers: Three proposed legal designations
Authorization letter from General Partner
Proof of identity of the General Partner's directors
Statement of principal activity (offshore towage and salvage services)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed designation is refused, revise the treaty, add a distinctive element, or file a reconsideration request under s. 32 of the Act; decide on a new proposal within 30 days of the refusal notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Limited Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal counsels and notaries in Quebec (notarization optional for non-real estate contributions)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and sign the convention de société en commandite or articles of limited partnership under arts. 2236-2246 CCQ; set out the General Partner (commandité), limited partners (commanditaires), capital subscription schedules, profit and loss sharing ratios, management powers of the General Partner, transfer restrictions, dissolution events, and appointment of a representative in Quebec resident for service of process.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of all partners (individuals and entities)
Capital subscription schedule and payment ledger
Registered office consent from the address provider
Power of attorney for the statutory representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a partner's eligibility is challenged (e.g., for foreign limited partners), amend the agreement by unanimous consent and re-execute signatures; variances are cured by a supplementary deed of amendment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the Declaration of Registration with REQ
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec - Directeur de l'immatriculation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Declaration of Registration electronically via REQ's Registrar en ligne portal; disclose the Partnership's exact legal name, head office address in Quebec, date of formation, identification of the General Partner with its own REQ number, the name and address of each limited partner where required, and the nature of the partnership business; sign electronically using the General Partner's credentials.
required_dossiers: Approved legal designation certificate
Executed limited partnership agreement
REQ online login credentials of the General Partner
Certified copy of the General Partner's board resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ issues a notice of non-conformity, respond with corrected particulars within 30 days; upon refusal, request a remedy from the Director or appeal to the Cour du Québec within 60 days of the refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - Business Registration Online and Revenu Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the REQ-registered partnership to obtain a federal Business Number (BN) via CRA's online registration; register for GST/HST (net 5% GST plus 9.975% QST collected by Revenu Québec), payroll program account, and corporate income tax account if applicable; register the Partnership with Revenu Québec for QST and with the Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST) for workplace accident insurance.
required_dossiers: REQ registration certificate (dated certificate of immatriculation)
Limited partnership agreement
General Partner's BN and CRA account details
Directors'/partners' contact information and tax PINs
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA rejects the application due to beneficiary ownership concerns (AML), amend the partnership agreement and beneficial ownership declaration; resubmit the corrected registration within 30 days and request a CRA service adjustment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Banking and Marine Trade Payment Rails
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Schedule I Canadian chartered bank (e.g., BMO, National Bank of Canada) and Transport Canada
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a commercial operating account in CAD and USD in the Partnership's name using the REQ certificate and partnership agreement; execute and sign banking declarations for Lloyd's Standard Form wire transfers (Look at Lloyd's Wreck and Salvage) and an escrow retention mandate for salvage awards; simultaneously initiate vessel flagging letters with Transport Canada Marine Safety and Security for future Canadian registration.
required_dossiers: REQ certificate of immatriculation (attested copy)
Executed limited partnership agreement and beneficial ownership schedule
General Partner's adoption resolution and officer ID
AML/KYC declarations with source of funds for towage operations
Escrow instruction letter and Lloyds wire template
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank issues a KYC query, provide a complete beneficial ownership chain of the General Partner and partners; if Transport Canada flags the declared vessel, file a corrected ownership declaration under the Canada Shipping Act, 2001.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Transport Canada Marine Safety and Security (TCMSS) - Marine Personnel and Vessel Registration Unit; Canadian Transportation Agency (for coasting trade licences)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Certificate of Registry for Tug and Salvage Vessels (Canada Shipping Act, 2001), Coasting Trade Licence under the Coasting Trade Act, and Marine Personnel Certificates of Competency for the crew

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) - Canadian Environmental Assessment Authority; Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs du Québec (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B - Registration (no full EIA designated project under the Impact Assessment Act for vessel towage and salvage operations unless shore-side infrastructure, such as a shipyard or permanent mooring facility, is constructed; under the Quebec Environmental Quality Act, a declaratory or attestation regime applies for port-side support works)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: MARPOL Annex I - oily water separator discharge limit of 15 ppm with zero visible sheen; sewage discharge prohibited within 3 nautical miles unless treated by an approved marine sanitation device under the Vessel Pollution and Dangerous Chemicals Regulations (SOR/2012-69); garbage and plastics retention on board; ballast water exchange at least 200 nautical miles from shore with a minimum depth of 200 metres; MARPOL Annex VI - fuel sulphur limit of 0.50% m/m outside Emission Control Areas and strict VOC emission control during bunkering.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Quebec civil security fire safety certificate (attestation de sécurité incendie) issued by the local fire department for any owned premises; CNESST workplace health and safety clearance including a written emergency response plan and hazardous materials inventory; structural load inspection certificate for berthing facilities per Quebec building regulations (Code du bâtiment); proof of a valid inland and coastal marine emergency plan approved by TCMSS for salvage operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) — federal GST/HST and income tax administration; Revenu Québec (RQ) — provincial QST, QPIP, and provincial income tax administration. Primary portals: CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) and CRA My Business Account; RQ 'Mon dossier d'entreprise' (CLIC); corporate/partnership registry: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) for the NEQ.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign limited partnership carrying on business in Quebec: (1) Apply to CRA for a 9-digit federal Business Number (BN) with the RC (GST/HST) program account via Form RC348 ('Request for a Business Number and Certain Program Accounts') or through the CRA BRO portal; (2) Register the extra-provincial limited partnership with the REQ to obtain the 10-character Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ); (3) Register for QST with Revenu Québec (Form LM-1-V) using the NEQ, obtaining a 15-digit QST registration number; (4) After registration, file the T5013 Partnership Information Return annually and remit GST/QST returns (GST34-1); non-resident partners report Canadian-source income under ITA s. 2(3)/115. Registration is mandatory once taxable supply thresholds are exceeded; the GST/HST registration effective date is the earlier of the first taxable supply and the application date.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — Quebec L.P. (société en commandite) is fiscally transparent for income tax purposes under ITA s. 96; income, gains, and losses flow through to partners pro rata. For GST/HST and QST the partnership is, however, treated as a separate 'person' registrant (ETA s. 123(1); Quebec Taxation Act). Territorial scope: resident partners taxed on worldwide income; non-resident partners taxed only on Canadian-source business income (ITA s. 2(3), 115) subject to treaty relief. No Quebec tax-exempt zone or special maritime zone applies to offshore towage/salvage operations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no US-style 'check-the-box' election; classification follows the Income Tax Act and ETA. Available elections include: (1) hybrid mismatch elections under ITA ss. 18.4(3) and 18.4(4) (Forms RC605 'P' and 'Q' elections) to treat certain hybrid entities as corporations or to neutralize deduction/non-inclusion mismatches, relevant to cross-border LP structures; (2) ETA s. 156 election for closely related registrants (limited application to an L.P. corporate general-partner group); (3) QST elections with Revenu Québec for associated persons and simplified accounting; (4) partnership fiscal-year elections (ITA s. 249.1) and CCA allocation elections in prescribed form.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Excise Tax Act, Part IX) plus Quebec QST (Quebec Taxation Act, Title III) — VAT-type consumption taxes. Quebec is not an HST province; the federal GST of 5% applies alongside the provincial QST of 9.975%, with QST computed on the GST-inclusive price.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 — small supplier threshold based on worldwide taxable supplies (excluding capital and financial services) in the current calendar quarter and the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters (ETA s. 148(1)); the same CAD 30,000 threshold applies for QST registration. Zero-rated export supplies count toward the threshold; registration is mandatory once exceeded and voluntary below it.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, API-based pre-clearance, or digital stamping regime exists in Canada. Invoicing must satisfy ETA s. 169(4) and s. 3 of the Information Returns Regulations (supplier name, BN/QST registration number, date, description, and tax particulars). Electronic invoices are accepted; the Pan-Canadian Peppol-based e-invoicing network is being adopted voluntarily for B2B/B2G. Quebec requires QST returns to be filed electronically through Revenu Québec's EDT system, but no pre-clearance of individual invoices is mandated.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under Schedule VI of the Excise Tax Act: (1) Part V, s. 1 — supplies of goods exported by the supplier, with prescribed evidence of exportation; (2) Part VII, s. 7(1) — supplies of transportation services (including freight towage) in respect of the movement of goods from a place in Canada to a place outside Canada; (3) Part V, s. 7 — supplies of services made to a non-resident client where the service is rendered wholly outside Canada or, with exceptions, where the performance is in Canada but the service is supplied to a non-resident and not in connection with taxable Canadian property. For offshore towage/salvage, services rendered on the high seas to non-resident shipowners or in support of international commercial shipping qualify for 0% GST and 0% QST; services performed within Canadian waters for Canadian-resident principals are taxable at the 5% GST + 9.975% QST rate unless a specific international-transportation exemption applies. The registrant must retain contemporaneous evidence to substantiate the non-resident destination and beneficial recipient.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Customs Export Declaration (CAERS/CAED) — Form B13A or electronic export reporting filed with the Canada Border Services Agency
Bill of Lading or sea waybill evidencing the international movement or destination of the towage/salvage operation
Signed towage/salvage contract (e.g., Lloyd's Open Form or BIMCO towage agreement) identifying the non-resident principal and scope
Commercial invoice and GST/QST invoice showing 0% tax applied and the supplier's BN/QST registration numbers
Foreign exchange remittance certificate or bank wire-transfer statement evidencing receipt of payment from the non-resident client
CRA Form GST11 (Certification of Export) or equivalent documentary evidence of exportation, where goods are moved as part of the supply
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec generally reassess within 4 years of the filing due date, with no limitation period in cases of misrepresentation, fraud, or gross negligence (ETA s. 296). Clawback: zero-rating is reversed and the taxpayer is assessed for unremitted GST/QST plus prescribed daily compound interest if evidence of export or non-resident status is absent or deficient. Penalties include: ETA s. 285(1) gross-negligence penalty equal to the greater of CAD 100 and 50% of net tax understated; s. 280 failure-to-file penalties; and criminal prosecution under s. 327 — summary conviction fines up to CAD 250,000 and 2 years' imprisonment, or indictment fines up to CAD 1,000,000 and 5 years' imprisonment. Quebec mirrors these sanctions under the Quebec Taxation Act and Tax Administration Act, with material penalty exposure for false or omitted statements connected to zero-rated marine claims.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada; foreign exchange and banking-system integrity functions are supplemented by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) and the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC); Quebec-level supervision is exercised through the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) for financial intermediaries.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible on both current and capital accounts. Canada maintains no exchange-control legislation; the former Foreign Exchange Control Act was repealed and no approval is required for inbound capital, outbound dividends, loan repayments, or profit remittances. For a Quebec Limited Partnership paying profits to non-resident partners, the principal constraint is Part XIII withholding tax under the Income Tax Act (Canada) and corresponding Quebec provincial withholdings, not currency convertibility. Escrowed salvage remuneration and Lloyd's Open Form awards may be paid in USD or CAD and converted freely.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory surrender, repatriation, or mandatory conversion requirements for export proceeds in Canada. A Quebec LP may retain offshore service revenue in foreign currency, maintain foreign-currency bank accounts domestically, or convert proceeds to CAD through licensed financial institutions. The only regulatory obligations are the standard FINTRAC anti-money-laundering reporting thresholds and tax-reporting/transfer-pricing documentation obligations under the Income Tax Act for cross-border transactions.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Transaction Account
Operational Transaction Account / Foreign Currency Account
Operational Transaction Account / SWIFT Treasury Account
Operational Transaction Account / International Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for settlement-only payment collection and low as a primary liquidity or escrow treasury vehicle. Offshore digital EMIs such as electronic-money institutions based in the UK/EEA do not hold Canadian banking licences under the Bank Act (Canada); they cannot take deposits, originate credit, or provide a Lloyd's-standard-form escrow security that Canadian maritime counterparties will accept. They may operate as money services businesses (MSBs) registered with FINTRAC and, once the Retail Payment Activities Act (Canada) fully applies, as registered payment service providers with the Bank of Canada. For the Quebec LP, an offshore EMI may be used for low-value cross-border collections, but not for LOF security deposits or capital escrow.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No Canadian federal statute expressly compels a physical in-branch appearance for account opening; however, Schedule I banks and Quebec-regulated institutions internally classify non-resident LPs in a high-risk category. The onboarding policy for the proposed CA_LP with an offshore towage/salvage business will require at least one general partner or senior operations officer to attend a physical KYC interview at a Quebec City or Montreal branch. Remote video verification is available only after a Canadian banking-relationship anchor account exists, and even then the final responsible officer may need to execute a bank-guarantee/escrow facility. A fully virtual opening with zero physical interview is not feasible for an offshore vessel-owning and salvage-operations structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident limited partnership with opaque beneficial ownership among silent partners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised limited partnership agreement; declaration of all persons with significant control (25% or more economic/control interest); corporate registry extracts for all corporate partners from the Quebec Registraire des entreprises; government-issued ID and residential proof for all general partners and beneficial owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Salvage and towage revenue flows triggered by Marine Emergency Case / Lloyd's Open Form arbitration
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Copy of the Lloyds Standard Form of Salvage Agreement; preliminary salvage security demand and cash escrow receipts; classification society and P&I insurance certificates; arbitration or admiralty settlement statements; independent invoice from the appointed salvage arbitrator/marine surveyor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border wire pattern with multi-currency payees, including tug owners, subcontractors, ports, and agents in jurisdictions subject to enhanced sanctions screening
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions screening reports covering UN, EU, OFAC, and Canadian (SEMA/UNACT) lists; detailed per-transaction commercial invoice matrix; vessel AIS logs and port-entry records; charter party or towage service contract; any required Transport Canada permits for international towing and salvage.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Escrowed third-party payments from shipowners' P&I clubs or legal counsel acting for foreign interests
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Kevin/escrow ledger records; P&I club security undertaking; law firm trust ledger slice for the LP; signed indemnity and release wording; full corporate legal opinion confirming the escrow purpose and non-possession of unidentified funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of ISIC 5222 / NAICS 488330 in a high-volume towage and salvage business with irregular revenue patterns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transport Canada maritime licence or exemption; Quebec inland-waters permit as applicable; ISPS/ROPE compliance certificates; multi-year audited financial statements or accountant-prepared operating ledgers; salvage indemnity caps and marine insurance programme summary.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections from non-resident limited partners must arrive to the Quebec LP via SWIFT MT103 from an owned-account in a recognised jurisdiction. The remittance field must use a clear purpose code, notably /UGT/ or /GIFT/ where appropriate, or the bank’s own business-purpose description, with reference to the LP’s Quebec registration number (NEQ). For example: Field 70: /PURP/TRADE; /LPIS/CA_LP; 'Capital contribution to Quebec LP for offshore towage and marine salvage operation'. The beneficiary must match the exact account name at the Canadian bank; funds may be held temporarily in a pre-funding account before transfer into the operating account. Verification includes confirming the sender’s bank is not subject to a Canadian sanctions measure and that the ultimate beneficial owners match the KYC-approved list.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade and operational disbursements should be cleared using SWIFT MT103 for standard supplier, subcontractor, bunker, and port payments; SWIFT MT202 Cover is reserved for bank-to-bank interbank positioning where required. For larger towage and salvage transactions, commercial letters of credit issued by a Schedule I Canadian bank are acceptable for financing purchases of tugs, equipment, or subcontractor services. Simultaneously, Lloyd's Open Form salvage awards and escrow releases should be settled through a dedicated Canadian law-firm escrow account via MT103 wire to the LP's National Bank of Canada operating account, referencing 'LOS-2025-Salvage-Settlement' and the arbitration case number. The rail instruction must include the approved batched invoice list to avoid failure in payments Canada
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable outright USD/CAD and EUR/CAD FX forwards under ISDA or standard Canadian bank treasury bilateral documentation
FX swaps combining a spot transaction with a reverse forward for settlement of trade invoices and escrow draws
Cross-currency swaps for long-term tug financing or multi-year salvage con-tract cash flows
European-vanilla FX options to hedge downward/upward margin protection on USD-denominated salvage awards

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only where the reference currency is a restricted/emerging-market currency and the CAD is used as settlement currency; deliverable forwards are the ordinary instrument for CAD/USD given Canada’s fully convertible currency

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) – Registraire des entreprises du Québec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days of each registration anniversary date (per REQ annual notice)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file for two consecutive years triggers administrative strike-off of the limited partnership; late-filing surcharge of CAD 30–300 may apply; revival fees and legal publicity blackout are imposed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return and T5013 Slips
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 31 for calendar-year fiscal periods; within 5 months after the end of non-calendar fiscal periods
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of CAD 24 per day per return, minimum CAD 100 and maximum CAD 2,500; gross negligence penalties apply; partners' deductions may be suspended.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is imposed on a Quebec limited partnership under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises. A certified audit is mandatory only if (i) required by the partnership agreement, (ii) ordered by the court upon a partner petition representing at least 10% of the partnership capital, or (iii) the partnership is a reporting issuer under securities legislation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: ASPE (CPA Canada Handbook – Part II) for private partnerships; IFRS (Part I) if publicly accountable or voluntarily elected; tax allocations follow the Income Tax Act and Quebec Taxation Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: For a Quebec limited partnership, the annual declaration to REQ confirms partner identity, contributions, and allocated percentages. Any change in partners or in the voting interest must be filed as a modification notice with REQ within 30 days. There is no separate standalone UBO annual filing; the partnership maintains a current partner register on site, subject to inspection and potential court-ordered audit.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners (general and limited) showing contributions, withdrawals, and share percentages
Minute Book containing partnership resolutions, consents, and manager mandates
Register of Statutory Declarations and Security Interests on partnership interests

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 180 – USD 650 (depending on agent tier and service scope)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 – USD 12,000 (if audit is voluntarily required or contractually mandated; no statutory audit otherwise)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined headline (federal 15.0% + Quebec 11.5%); 0% entity-level tax because the limited partnership is fiscally transparent and assesses each partner on allocable income.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday for offshore towage or salvage. Income is eligible for generally applicable deductions: capital cost allowance, Quebec/Federal credits for qualified marine operations where available, and the Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) small business deduction on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income (combined 14.0% federal/Quebec rate) when the partner is a CCPC.
